source_text: Et occulta tenebrarum ipse inluminabit, utique per Christum, qui Christum in lumen nationum repromisit quique se lucernam pronuntiauit scrutantem renes et corda. ab illo erit et laus unicuique, a quo et contrarium laudis, ut a iudice. certe, inquis, uel hic mundum deum mundi interpretatur dicendo: spectaculum facti sumus mundo, et angelis et hominibus, quia, si mundum homines mundi significasset, non etiam homines postmodum nominasset. immo, ne ita argumentareris, prouidentia spiritus sancti demonstrauit, quomodo dixisset: spectaculum facti sumus mundo, dum angelis, qui mundo ministrant, et hominibus, quibus ministrant. uerebatur nimirum tantae constantiae uir, ne dicam spiritus sanctus, praesertim ad filios scribens, quos in euangelio generauerat, libere deum mundi nominare, aduersus <quem) nisi exerte non posset uideri praedicare. non defendo secundum legem creatoris displicuisse illum, qui mulierem patris sui habuit — communis et publicae religionis secutus sit disciplinam —: sed cum eum damnat dedendum satanae, damnatoris dei praeco, est. uiderit et quomodo dixerit: in interitum carnis, ut spiritus saluus sit in die domini, dum et de carnis interitu et de salute spiritus iudicarit et \'auferri\' iubens \'malum de medio\' creatoris frequentissimam sententiam commemorauerit. Expurgate uetus fermentum, ut sitis noua consparsio, sicut estis azymi. ergo azymi figurae erant nostrae apud creatorem. sic et pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus. quare pascha Christus, si non pascha figura Christi per similitudinem sanguinis salutaris pecoris et Christi? quid nobis et Christo imagines induit sollemnium creatoris, si non erant nostrae? Auertens autem nos a fornicatione manifestat carnis resurrectionem. corpus, inquit, non fornicationi, sed domino, et dominus corpori, 'ut templum deo et deus templo\'. templum ergo deo peribit et deus templo? atquin uides: quem deus suscitauit et nos suscitabit, in corpore quoque suscitauit, quia corpus domino et dominus corpori. et bene quod aggerat: nescitis corpora uestra membra esse Christi?
pass_a_gloss: And He Himself will illuminate the hidden things of darkness, certainly through Christ, who promised Christ as a light to the nations and who declared Himself a lamp examining kidneys and hearts. And there will be praise for each one from Him, from whom also the opposite of praise comes, so that from the judge. Certainly, you say, or does this God of the world interpret, saying: we have become a spectacle to the world, and to angels and to men, because if he had meant the world of men, he would not have named men afterwards as well. On the contrary, lest you argue in this way, the providence of the Holy Spirit demonstrated how He spoke: we have become a spectacle to the world, while to angels who minister to the world, and to men to whom they minister. This man of great constancy was certainly afraid, or rather the Holy Spirit, especially when writing to the sons whom he had generated in the gospel, to freely name the God of the world, against whom, unless openly, he could not be seen to preach. I do not defend the fact that according to the law of the Creator, it was displeasing that he who had his father's wife - following the discipline of a common and public religion -: but when he condemns him to be handed over to Satan, he is a herald of the God who condemns. Let him see how he says: to the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord, while he also judges both the destruction of the flesh and the salvation of the spirit, and commanding 'to take away' 'evil from the midst', he recalls the most frequent sentence of the Creator. Purge the old leaven, so that you may be a new mixture, just as you are unleavened. Therefore, the unleavened bread was a figure of ours with the Creator. So also our Passover, Christ, has been immolated. Why is Christ our Passover, if not the Passover, a figure of Christ, through the likeness of the saving blood of the animal and of Christ? What does it mean for us and for Christ to be given images of the Creator's solemnities, if they were not ours? But turning us away from fornication, He manifests the resurrection of the flesh. The body, he says, is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body, 'so that it may be a temple of God and God a temple'. Therefore, will the temple of God perish, and God the temple? But you see: whom God has raised, and will raise us, He has also raised in the body, because the body is for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body. And it is good that he adds: do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ?

pass_b_english: God Himself will illuminate the hidden things of darkness, certainly through Christ, who promised Christ as a light to the nations and declared Himself a lamp examining kidneys and hearts. Praise will come to each person from Him, from whom the opposite of praise also comes, so that it comes from the judge.

You say, 'Does this God of the world interpret by saying: we have become a spectacle to the world, and to angels and to men?' Because if he had meant the world of men, he would not have named men afterwards as well. On the contrary, lest you argue that way, the providence of the Holy Spirit demonstrated how He spoke: we have become a spectacle to the world, while to angels who minister to the world, and to men to whom they minister. This man of such great constancy was certainly afraid — or rather the Holy Spirit was — especially when writing to the sons whom he had generated in the gospel, to freely name the God of the world, against whom, unless openly, he could not be seen to preach.

I do not defend the fact that, according to the law of the Creator, it was displeasing that he who had his father's wife — following the discipline of a common and public religion — : but when he condemns him to be handed over to Satan, he is a herald of the God who condemns. Let him see how he says: to the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord, while he judges both the destruction of the flesh and the salvation of the spirit, and, commanding 'to take away' 'evil from the midst,' he recalls the most frequent sentence of the Creator. Purge the old leaven, so that you may be a new mixture, just as you are unleavened (1 Corinthians 5:7). Therefore, the unleavened bread was a figure of ours with the Creator. So also our Passover, Christ, has been immolated. Why is Christ our Passover, if not because the Passover was a figure of Christ, through the likeness of the saving blood of the animal and of Christ? What does it mean for us and for Christ to be given images of the Creator's solemnities, if they were not ours?

But turning us away from fornication, He manifests the resurrection of the flesh. The body, he says, is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body, 'so that it may be a temple of God and God a temple' (1 Corinthians 6:19). Therefore, will the temple of God perish, and God the temple? But you see: whom God has raised, and will raise us, He has also raised in the body, because the body is for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body. And it is good that he adds: do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ?
